newsitem.title: CHILE: British explorer forced to give up Antarctic trek.
newsitem.headline: British explorer forced to give up Antarctic trek.

text.p: British explorer Sir Ranulph Fiennes was hospitalized Friday suffering from a serious case of kidney stones that forced him to abandon his solo walk across Antarctica.

Fiennes, after walking some 250 miles (400 km) across Antarctica on a walk to benefit breast cancer research, was evacuated Thursday to a hospital in the Chilean city of Punta Arena, a hospital official said.

"Sir Ranulph has been in excrutiating pain for the last 48 hours suffering from kidney stones. The stone has now become stuck and therefore needs to be surgically removed," said a statement issued by the mission's London organisers, Dyson Antarctica Solo.
Organisers say Fiennes' walk would have been the first solo, unsupported trek across the frozen continent.
He alerted rescuers via radio contact and activitated his satellite location beacons to let them where he was when he needed to be rescued, said the statement.
